figures.finding: Under Burundi's civil law majority is at twenty-one (Code of Persons and the Family, arts. 335 and 337), as the Government reported in 2008, noting it hadn't yet aligned the age with the Convention's eighteen.
figures.applies: Burundi; the State's report of 2008. Whether a later reform lowered it wasn't established.

sources.said: Under civil law, the age of majority is 21 years.

figures.finding: The 1993 Labour Code set the minimum age for admission to employment at sixteen; a 1981 ministerial order lets children under sixteen work where the work doesn't harm schooling or health, and lists barred work; labour inspectors may require a doctor's examination.

value.under16: allowed under the 1981 ministerial order if not harmful to schooling or health
